extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and applicants preparing/submitting nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings to the USPTO (including PCT filers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural guidance for preparing and filing nucleotide/amino acid "Sequence Listing" documents and their computer-readable forms (CRF) with the USPTO and in PCT international applications, including file format, size limits, labeling, required statements, and consequences of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission as ASCII plain text file (.txt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System, applicants may submit a “Sequence Listing” under 37 CFR 1.821 as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; each text file must be an ASCII plain text file and have a file name with a ".txt" extension. See 37 CFR 1.824.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recommends submitting the Sequence Listing as ASCII plain text rather than as a PDF image file. An ASCII plain text file submitted via the electronic filing system will serve as both the Sequence Listing under 37 CFR 1.821(c) and the CRF under 37 CFR 1.821(e) provided no PDF/image copy or paper copy is also filed. Do not compress the .txt file when submitting via EFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference statement when using ASCII file
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants submitting a Sequence Listing as an ASCII plain text file must include a statement in the specification in a separate paragraph (preferably on the first page) that incorporates by reference the material in the ASCII plain text file identifying the name of the file, date of creation, and size in bytes (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5) and 1.823(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: an incorporation-by-reference statement is not required in an international application or in an application under 35 U.S.C. 371 where the Sequence Listing was previously communicated to the International Bureau or originally filed in the USPTO and complies with PCT Rule 5.2 (see 37 CFR 1.821(c), 1.825(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit duplicate PDF/paper copies when ASCII file is used
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing is submitted as an ASCII plain text file in compliance with 37 CFR 1.824 via the EFS and applicant has not filed a Sequence Listing as a PDF image file or on physical sheets of paper, the ASCII plain text file will serve as both the Sequence Listing and the CRF; therefore a second copy as a PDF image or on paper is not required and should not be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting PDF/image or paper copies when an acceptable ASCII .txt is provided may cause those copies to be counted for application size fees. Avoid submitting duplicates to prevent fee or processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-readable form (CRF) required when listing is PDF or paper
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.821(e) requires submission of a copy of the Sequence Listing in computer readable form (CRF) in a US application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or in a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371 when the Sequence Listing is submitted as a PDF image file or on physical sheets of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRF must be submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc(s) as permitted by 37 CFR 1.824(b). If a Sequence Listing is filed as paper or PDF, submit a separate CRF copy; if the ASCII plain text file is used, it serves as both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing serves as CRF when filed as ASCII via EFS
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Sequence Listing is submitted in compliance with 37 CFR 1.824 as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO EFS, the ASCII file will serve as both the Sequence Listing under 37 CFR 1.821(c) and the CRF under 37 CFR 1.821(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eliminates the need for a separate CRF and avoids inclusion of the sequence listing in application size/sheet counts (see application size fee rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee exclusion for ASCII plain text Sequence Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Sequence Listing or CRF submitted as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO EFS that is in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821(c) or (e) will be excluded when determining the application size fee required by 37 CFR 1.16(s) or 1.492(j) as per 37 CFR 1.52(f)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Sequence Listing submitted as a PDF image file via EFS or on read-only optical disc will not be excluded when determining the application size fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 100 megabyte size limit for Sequence Listing ASCII text files
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred (100) megabytes is the size limit for Sequence Listing ASCII plain text files submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, and compression is not allowed for a Sequence Listing submitted via EFS. See 37 CFR 1.824(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence Listing files may not be partitioned into multiple files to circumvent the limit; any Sequence Listing greater than 100 MB must be submitted on read-only optical disc(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Sequence Listings exceeding 100 MB
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing exceeds 100 MB, it is recommended to file the application without the Sequence Listing via EFS to obtain the application/confirmation number, then file the Sequence Listing on read-only optical disc(s) (in accordance with 37 CFR 1.52(e) and 1.824) the same day by Priority Mail Express® or hand delivery to secure the same filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read-only optical discs must contain a single (uncompressed) file, or if compressed/split for multiple discs, must be labeled with inventor, title, docket, application number/filing date (if known), date recorded on disc, and disc order (e.g., '1 of X'). Also note: electronic submissions of 300 MB or more may be subject to oversized submission fees under 37 CFR 1.21(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mega-sequence listing fee treatment (300 MB and larger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions of very lengthy sequence listings (300 MB or over, a.k.a. mega-sequence listings) in international applications are not subject to the mega-sequence listing submission fees set forth in 37 CFR 1.21(o); however, mega-sequence listings received in national stage applications or certain other contexts on or after specified dates may be subject to the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee applicability depends on filing context (international vs national stage) and filing date; consult 37 CFR 1.21(o) and MPEP text for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Tables and Computer Program Listing Appendix limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The current EFS size limit for ASCII plain text submissions of 'Large Tables' and a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' is 25 megabytes per submission, and compression is not allowed for these items when submitted via EFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files above 25 MB may be broken into multiple files no larger than 25 MB each (file names must indicate order, e.g., '1 of X') or submitted on read-only optical disc(s). If larger than 25 MB, consider filing the application first and then submitting the large files on optical disc the same day to secure the same filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing must be a separate part of the description in PCT filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Rule 5.2(a), where an international application contains nucleotide/amino acid sequences, the description shall contain a sequence listing complying with the Administrative Instructions and presented as a separate part of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a PCT international application via the USPTO EFS, it is highly recommended to submit the sequence listing as a single ASCII plain text file with a ".txt" extension on the international filing date. Although not recommended, a PDF image may be submitted, but an ASCII file is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: single ASCII file and effect on inclusion in international application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sequence listing is submitted as an ASCII plain text file with the PCT filing, the ASCII file will serve as both the sequence listing part of the description required under PCT Rule 5.2 and the electronic form under PCT Rule 13ter.1(a) in the absence of a PDF sequence listing file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit additional copies if ASCII is used. If both PDF image and ASCII are filed but Box No. IX does not indicate which one forms part of the application, the PDF will be considered to form part of the application and the ASCII as an accompanying item for search only.

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing fee and sheet count depend on file type
rubrics_metrics.description: The international filing fee for a PCT application that includes a sequence listing is calculated based on the type of sequence listing file that is part of the description. An ASCII plain text file will not be included in the sheet count; a PDF image file will be included when it is part of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing both PDF (as part of description) and ASCII (for search only), the sheets of the PDF image file will count towards excess sheet fees, if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements required when adding Sequence Listing after filing (PCT Rule 13ter / 37 CFR 1.821(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a user adds a Sequence Listing (under PCT Rule 13ter) as an ASCII plain text file via EFS in response to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.821(h), the ASCII file must be accompanied by a statement that the ASCII plain text file does not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed and the late furnishing fee under 37 CFR 1.445(a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sequence listing is provided in reply to 1.821(h), include the required statement and pay the late furnishing fee. Failure to do so may affect search/examination treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments adding/replacing Sequence Listings must comply with 37 CFR 1.825
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant files an amendment to comply with 37 CFR 1.821(g) that adds or replaces a Sequence Listing and CRF copy thereof, the amendment must be submitted in accordance with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide a proper reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.825 will result in abandonment of the application. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 may be available; delays may affect patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of identity between Sequence Listing and CRF when CRF is separate
rubrics_metrics.description: When a separate CRF is submitted because the Sequence Listing is filed as a PDF image file or on physical sheets (or in certain national stage situations), 37 CFR 1.821(e)(1)(ii)/(2)(ii) require a statement that the information contained in the Sequence Listing and the separate CRF are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a statement may be made by a registered practitioner, the applicant, an inventor, or the person who actually compares the sequence data. Sample statements are provided in MPEP § 2428.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF data entry, exchange, and non-return of optical media
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the CRF will be entered into the Office's database for searching and to enable exchange with NCBI/GenBank, DDBJ, and EBI. Once the Office has entered the data, it does not intend to permanently preserve the CRF submitted on read-only optical disc(s) and applicants should not expect discs to be returned. See 37 CFR 1.52(e)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that CRF data will be used to populate public databases only when the application publishes or issues; unpublished pending application sequences are maintained separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and discrepancies between Sequence Listing and CRF
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may permit correction of the Sequence Listing (paper or PDF) by reference to the CRF if both were submitted at filing and the totality of circumstances substantiate the proposed correction; a mere discrepancy may not by itself justify correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office assumes the CRF has been incorporated by reference when both were submitted at filing. The applicant bears the burden to eliminate or minimize discrepancies and may suffer consequences of any remaining discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-compliance with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.821(g) requires compliance with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.821(b) through (e) within the period set in a notice; failure to comply (including failure to submit proper amendment per 1.825) will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance may also affect patent term adjustment (reductions) if not in condition for examination within eight months. International applications failing to satisfy 1.821(e)(3) may be searched/examined only to the extent possible without CRF information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to avoid introduction of new matter when amending sequence information
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to submit statements assuring no new matter (e.g., that a submission does not go beyond the disclosure or that CRF is identical) is analogous to the substitute specification rule; the burden is on applicant to ensure no new matter is added. Corrections of sequencing or descriptive errors are subject to statutory prohibitions against new matter (35 U.S.C. 132 and 251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure amendments, replacements, or late-filed sequence listings do not introduce new matter; statements required in PCT/national replies may be signed by qualified persons (practitioner, applicant, inventor, or comparator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions regarding compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither presence nor absence of information not required under the sequence rules creates a presumption that such information is necessary to satisfy any of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112. Further, the grant of a patent on an application subject to 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 constitutes a presumption that the granted patent complies with these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies evidentiary effect but does not relieve applicants of their burden to comply with the rules during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and code set for sequence characters (37 CFR 1.822(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The code for representing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence characters shall conform to the code set forth in appendices A and C to this subpart; no other code shall be used. A modified base or modified/unusual amino acid may be presented as the corresponding unmodified residue if listed in appendices B or D and the modification is set forth in the Feature section; otherwise use 'n' or 'Xaa' respectively and provide further information in Feature section with feature keys from appendices E and F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices A–F correspond to WIPO ST.25 tables; ensure use of the specified codes and include Feature section entries for modifications or unusual residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide sequence formatting rules (grouping, coding, line length, direction, enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences shall use lowercase one-letter codes (appendix A). Bases in noncoding parts are listed in groups of 10 (with leftover <10 grouped at end) separated by spaces; bases in coding parts are listed as triplets (codons) with corresponding amino acids listed immediately below codons. Maximum 16 codons or 60 bases per line with spaces between codons/groups. Sequences represented by a single strand in 5' to 3' direction, left to right. Enumeration starts at first base number 1 and continues through sequence; enumeration appears in right margin next to the line and gives number of last base on that line. For circular sequences, enumeration method remains applicable but designation of first base may be at applicant's option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a codon spans an intron the amino acid symbol is listed below the portion of the codon containing two nucleotides. Follow precise spacing and numbering requirements to conform to 37 CFR 1.822(c)(1)–(7).
